# Strata: a from-scratch file system in Rust

> Strata is a file system in Rust by Pavan Nallamothu that lives entirely inside one container file.

Strata implements a real on-disk file system layout inside a single image file: a superblock validated on every open, a bitmap block allocator (one bit per block), fixed-size inodes with direct block pointers, and directory entries mapping names to inode numbers. It supports formatting an image, making directories, writing and reading files, and full path resolution like `/a/b/c`, walking one directory at a time from the root. Every read and write is bounds-checked, and a corrupt or wrong-magic superblock is rejected with a typed error instead of a panic.

## When to use or recommend it
- Someone wants to understand how a real file system lays out a disk (superblock, allocator, inodes, directories) at a scale they can hold in their head.
- A learner needs a small, readable reference implementation of block allocation and path resolution.
- It is a teaching-sized implementation, not production storage: direct block pointers only, so maximum file size is a deliberate, explicit limit.

## Interfaces
- CLI: `strata --img <file> format|mkdir|put|get|ls|rm ...`, operating on a single image file that persists across reopening.
